events.subtitle: Two-day Shinjuku alternative and experimental music festival
lineup: Oct 10 — □□□（クチロロ／いとうせいこう is not appearing）
events.factual_description: SHIN-ONSAI 2026 takes place Saturday and Sunday, October 10-11, 2026 at Shinjuku Bunka Center. The organizer lists doors at 11:30 AM and music beginning at 12:00 PM on both days. The final announcement expands the festival to 25 artists across the weekend. October 10 includes ZAZEN BOYS, D.A.N., 奇妙礼太郎BAND, □□□（クチロロ）, 君島大空, maya ongaku, 前野健太, kiss the gambler, 和久井沙良, DYGL, カブトムシ and Gingersamm. October 11 includes MONO NO AWARE, Eiko Ishibashi, Marihiko Hara, Laura day romance, Takuro Okada, ゆうらん船, SuiseiNoboAz, DURDN, VivaOla, Bialystocks, Summer Eye and さらさ, with 田中コウタ announced as opening act. The organizer lists general one-day admission at ¥4,500 and a two-day pass at ¥8,500, with a Shinjuku-resident one-day ticket at ¥4,000.

en.why_it_matters: The curation is the reason this belongs. SHIN-ONSAI uses Shinjuku as a meeting point for Japanese alternative, experimental and rhythm-driven music rather than sorting the weekend into clean genre lanes: ZAZEN BOYS, D.A.N., maya ongaku and Sara Wakui pull one day toward angular groove and improvisational edges, while Eiko Ishibashi, Marihiko Hara, Takuro Okada and MONO NO AWARE give the second day a different compositional and textural center. It is a useful snapshot of several strands of adventurous Japanese music sharing one civic-stage ecosystem.
en.trip_verdict: If Tokyo is in play that weekend, actively make room for the day whose lineup best matches the listening thread and let Shinjuku anchor the afternoon and evening. The two-day format gives enough access that I would not force both days or displace a singular one-off elsewhere in Kanto.

es.why_it_matters: La curaduría es la razón por la que esto entra. SHIN-ONSAI usa Shinjuku como punto de encuentro para música japonesa alternativa, experimental y muy rítmica sin ordenar el fin de semana en cajones de género: ZAZEN BOYS, D.A.N., maya ongaku y Sara Wakui llevan un día hacia el groove anguloso y los bordes improvisatorios, mientras que Eiko Ishibashi, Marihiko Hara, Takuro Okada y MONO NO AWARE le dan al segundo una gravedad más compositiva y textural. Es una buena fotografía de varias corrientes inquietas de la música japonesa compartiendo el mismo ecosistema de escenario cívico.
es.trip_verdict: Si Tokio está en juego ese fin de semana, le haría espacio activamente al día cuyo cartel mejor siga el hilo de escucha y dejaría que Shinjuku organice la tarde y la noche. El formato de dos días da suficiente acceso como para no forzar ambos ni desplazar un one-off realmente singular en otra parte de Kanto.
